name: Sonnet+tools deep value
strategy: Global deep-value dividend payers - single-digit-to-low-teens P/E, near-book P/B, strong FCF, durable 6%+ dividends across tobacco, telecom, financials, pharma and autos - now with the packaged-food leg cut on credible dividend-cut risk and cash raised as ballast.
reassessment_note: The book is up +3.74% since inception, slightly ahead of SPY (+3.62%), and five of six legs are doing exactly what a deep-value dividend book is supposed to do - VZ +7.11%, PFE +13.75%, C +4.51% and MO +0.80% are working, and BTI's -8.74% mark-to-market is a valuation call getting cheaper, not a thesis break (no negative catalyst found this week, just multi-year regulatory overhang and a broad tobacco/staples wobble - 90-day BTI drawdown of 13.4% against an unchanged 49%-undervaluation and 10.6x forward P/E read as an opportunity for a value book, not an exit signal). KHC is different in kind: this week's Q2 print paired an EPS beat with a guided-down 2026 outlook, price cuts taken into a guidance cut (margin self-harm, not strength), and the CEO's own comment that consumers are 'literally running out of money' by month-end - the same macro stress that just drove peer Campbell to cut its dividend 36%. My mandate is 'durable 6%+ dividends,' and durability is precisely the assumption that just broke for this leg; a KHC dividend cut is now a real, not tail, risk. I am exiting the KHC 9% rather than holding into an event my own diligence flags as newly live. I am not chasing PFE further - it has run to +13.75%, patent-cliff risk is unchanged, and the average analyst target ($28.61) is now essentially at the market price ($28.45), so the easy re-rating is behind it; trimming 1pt funds a 1pt add to Citigroup, whose blowout Q2 and a market now pushing its first Fed cut out to June 2027 favor bank net-interest income for longer, and whose average analyst target ($154.50) still implies ~12% upside from $137.72 - the best remaining upside-to-conviction ratio in the book. VZ and MO are unchanged: VZ's yield (5.59%) and TD Cowen's raised $56 target still support the position even near its 52-week high, and MO's 61st consecutive dividend increase and 6.39% yield outweigh a single Barclays underweight call against a $70 average target. Net effect: same mandate, one leg removed for a fundamental reason (not a price move), cash raised from 23% to 32% as ballast, and the proceeds otherwise recycled toward the leg with the most analyst-upside-per-dollar-of-risk rather than into anything outside the value/income mandate.

positions.thesis: Unchanged 20% core position. Forward yield 5.59% ($2.83/sh), 13.1x trailing P/E, and TD Cowen raised its target to $56 (from $54) on 7/27 versus today's $50.14 close - the dividend-sustainability bears are outnumbered by upgraders even as the stock sits near its 52-week high. No earnings until 10/20/26, so no near-term catalyst risk; holding the winner.

Unchanged 17%. Just declared its 61st dividend increase in 57 years ($1.11/sh, ex-date 9/15) and yields 6.39% - the definition of the durable-dividend mandate. Barclays' Underweight ($58 target) is the outlier against a $70 average street target; on!-driven smoke-free pivot gives a real (if narrow) growth lever beyond pure cigarette decline. Holding at target size.

Increased from 12% to 13%, funded by the PFE trim. Blowout Q2 already booked (+4.51% leg P&L), 10.3x forward P/E, and this week's macro repricing - strong August payrolls (162k) pushed Citigroup's own house forecast for the first Fed cut out to June 2027 - is a tailwind for bank net-interest margin, not a headwind. Truist's Buy and the $154.50 average target imply ~12% upside from $137.72, the best remaining upside-to-risk in the book.

Unchanged 10% despite being the worst leg (-8.74%). Diligence this week found no company-specific negative catalyst behind the 13.4% 90-day slide - just sector-wide tobacco/staples weakness - while the valuation case got only cheaper: 10.6x forward P/E and a screen-flagged ~49% undervaluation gap versus peers. A deep-value book that sells its cheapest, still-thesis-intact name purely on price action is not doing deep value; holding size and letting the yield compound while it re-rates.

Trimmed from 9% to 8%, best performer this year (+13.75%) on FDA approval of the updated COVID vaccine, but the easy re-rating looks done: average analyst target ($28.61) is now essentially at the $28.45 close, Guggenheim just cut its target to $31 from $35, and the 2028 patent-cliff overhang (Eliquis, Ibrance) is unchanged. Keeping most of the position for the dividend and pipeline optionality, recycling the trim into higher-upside C.
